misconceptions.description: Applying statics equilibrium to a dynamic particle
misconceptions.trigger: learner sets sum F equal to zero despite nonzero acceleration
misconceptions.feedback: In dynamics, the net force does not need to vanish. If the object is accelerating, the correct target is sum F = m a, not sum F = 0.

misconceptions.description: Assigning friction based on preferred axis rather than actual sliding direction
misconceptions.trigger: learner places friction in the wrong direction on an incline or horizontal surface
misconceptions.feedback: Kinetic friction opposes the relative motion at the contact. Decide how the object is sliding first, then point friction opposite that motion.

misconceptions.description: Assuming the normal force always equals the full weight
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses N = mg on an incline without justification
misconceptions.feedback: The normal force equals the component of the weight perpendicular to the surface only when there is no acceleration through the surface. On an incline, that is usually N = mg cos(theta).

misconceptions.description: Confusing the sign of acceleration with the direction of velocity
misconceptions.trigger: learner assumes a moving-right object must also have positive acceleration
misconceptions.feedback: Velocity tells you the current direction of motion. Acceleration tells you how velocity is changing. An object can move right while having negative acceleration if it is slowing down.
